research_concepts: role portability across team or context moves
methodological_questions: Can role portability be tested with n=24 units at useful power?
How should cut-heavy and drive-heavy shaper roles be classified from play-by-play data?
How should portability be measured without deriving the label from the same outcome used to test it?
How should regression to the mean, landing-spot quality and small-sample instability be controlled?

historical_evidence.finding: Closest prior study. On 92 connector movers, pre-move cut share predicted whether a connector's organizational function reproduced after a move (cut share rho=+0.265, p=0.011, AUC 0.653; cut-minus-drive rho=+0.314, p=0.002; drive rho=-0.278, p=0.007). Top cut tercile was 65% portable (median Delta +0.167) vs bottom 35% (median -0.039). LOO AUC 0.622; permutation p=0.005 from 5000 label shuffles. Record notes the drop-Gafford and top-3 checks and position splits. Its own limitation tags are LIM:small_sample and RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

Connector diet x destination structural-gap match. Binary match rate 15.7%. Taxonomy connector subset n=19 gave delta match vs mismatch median +0.540 vs +0.069, p=0.156. Travel-check delta p=0.413. All-movers binary delta p=0.0283 (n=198) did not replicate as a continuous Spearman, which was -0.034 with p recorded as 0. Verdict null; failure type A_unanswerable; limited by LIM:small_sample.

DRIVE-as-BEST counter versus constrained mix, n=44. Observed gap -0.066 PPP (p=0.2175 vs B_fixed) with MDE 0.180 PPP at 80% power (SD about 0.34; 0.265 if SD about 0.5). Record states n=44 cannot distinguish a true null from an effect up to 0.18 PPP. Limited by LIM:low_power_large_MDE and LIM:small_sample.

Destination net-rating checks for movers (archive). Recorded result: 'underpowered and null once corrected for landing-spot quality', with no numbers. Dropped from Paper 1. Failure type A_unanswerable; limited by LIM:low_power_large_MDE and LIM:small_sample; related family FAM:SF-PAP-032.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Testing a diet-match or structural-gap-match binary against post-move delta in connector subsets and all movers
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable with LIM:small_sample. Connector subset was n=19; the all-movers binary result (p=0.0283) did not hold as a continuous Spearman, which was reported with p=0, so the result is fragile and not the licensed connector test.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting a DRIVE-based H2 PPP advantage over feasibility-constrained baselines
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable with LIM:low_power_large_MDE. The observed gap was smaller than the MDE of 0.180 PPP at n=44, so the test could not distinguish a true null from a meaningful effect.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using destination on-court net-rating change to check whether portability relates to outcomes
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as A_unanswerable and underpowered. The null result was reported only after correcting for landing-spot quality, and no sample or effect numbers were recorded. Dropped from Paper 1.

evidence_establishes: Earlier work by this project (FAM:SF-CHT-057) reported a positive cut-share association with post-move portability in a 92-mover sample, with a permutation-based p-value and a leave-one-out AUC of 0.622.

Three other attempts in the same area (FAM:SF-APPS-090, FAM:SF-APPS-024, FAM:SF-PAP-029) were recorded as untestable because of small samples or large minimum detectable effects. Sample size and power were the dominant recorded failure mode in this area.
Destination-quality confounding was recorded as material in FAM:SF-PAP-029, where the null was reported only after correction for landing-spot quality.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether the cut-versus-drive portability effect holds in the stated 2022-23 to 2025-26 NBA data. No record uses this data version, and the retrieved records do not state the same source or unit definitions.
Whether a 24-unit design has adequate power. None of the records covers n=24, and the closest sample (n=92) is about four times larger.
The replication status of FAM:SF-CHT-057. Its leave-one-out and permutation results are recorded, but no independent replication is recorded and its outcome is a derived delta.

Whether the portability outcome in SF-CHT-057 can be reconstructed from the current per-game files. Data-catalog fields for mover identity, pre-move and post-move context, and destination quality were not checked.
The stability of the Spearman p=0 result in FAM:SF-APPS-090, which is recorded but not explained.
own_inferences: If the 24 units are team-seasons or single moves, the sample is too small to detect an effect of the size that the closest prior study reported (AUC about 0.65), let alone a smaller one.

Pooling to player-level mover-seasons across 2022-23 to 2025-26 would be needed to approach the 92-mover scale of FAM:SF-CHT-057, and the pooled design must address the same destination-quality confound recorded in FAM:SF-PAP-029.

Defining cut versus drive shares from the same play-by-play used to derive portability, or using post-move outcomes to choose the classification threshold, would create a circular label and inflate the apparent effect.
A cut-versus-drive classification rule must be fixed before outcomes are examined. Otherwise the tercile split in SF-CHT-057 is a researcher degree of freedom.
uncertainties: The definition of the 24 units is not stated (player, team, move, or season-level), so the effective sample size is unknown.

Whether the NBA 2025-26 regular-season and playoff data used here is complete for the intended test. Per the stated availability, regular-season data is complete from 2026-04-13 and playoff data from 2026-06-21; earlier pulls would be partial.

The portability construct used in SF-CHT-057 (an organizational function reproducing after a move) is not defined in the retrieved records, so it may not map onto the per-game variables available here.
Measurement reliability of the cut-share and drive-share classification from play-by-play action types and sub-types is not reported in any retrieved record.
No validation or replication status is recorded for SF-CHT-057 beyond the auto-generated 'supported' label.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved evidence showed that the closest prior study (SF-CHT-057) had a supported positive result, but at n=92, and that three related attempts were untestable because of power or sample problems. Together with the stated n=24, this moved the decision from a possible test of the question as posed to a do-not-proceed recommendation for the question as posed. The minimum viable test below is the only version that could be considered.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 units is far below the 92-mover sample of the closest prior study, and the related records were recorded as underpowered (MDE of 0.18 PPP at n=44). A test at n=24 cannot reliably detect an effect of the size previously reported.

Destination structural quality is recorded as a confounder (FAM:SF-PAP-029 null only after correction for landing-spot quality). Without a measure of destination quality the cut-versus-drive contrast is confounded with where players land.

Portability is a post-move delta. If the cut/drive classification or the portable/not-portable label is derived from the same outcome, the test is circular, as the tercile analysis in SF-CHT-057 would be vulnerable to this.
The cut and drive shares depend on play-by-play action and sub-type coding. Their stability across seasons and across the playoff/regular-season split is not recorded in any retrieved record.

prior_work.summary: FAM:SF-CHT-057 reports a supported positive cut-share association with post-move portability in a 92-mover sample, which partly answers the question for a different sample and possibly a different outcome definition. The other three records are untestable for sample or power reasons and do not answer the question. Nothing retrieved tests the question with n=24 units or with the 2022-23 to 2025-26 data described here.

risks.text: n=24 units gives very low power. The closest prior study needed 92 movers, and related attempts with n=19 to 44 were recorded as underpowered.
Landing-spot quality and team context are recorded confounders. Without adjustment the cut-versus-drive effect may reflect where players moved rather than their role.
If the role classification or the portable label uses post-move outcomes, the association is partly built in.
Shares of cut and drive possessions from play-by-play coding may be unstable across seasons, and the playoff sample is smaller than the regular season.

The question is one of several role-type comparisons in this area, and the SF-CHT-057 result depends on a choice of cut-minus-drive, tercile, and position splits. Without pre-specification the reported p-values are inflated.
The permutation test in SF-CHT-057 used label shuffles. Its validity depends on whether shuffles preserve the dependence between roles, team and destination, so the placebo may be too weak.
Across 2022-23 to 2025-26, team-building, rule and pace changes may shift what cut and drive play types mean, so a pooled portability estimate could mix regimes.
The portable/not-portable label depends on how post-move function is defined; mislabeling of movers or misidentified role transitions would bias the contrast.

design.estimand: Difference in post-move portability (change in organizational function, Delta) between cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers, adjusted for pre-move role share and destination structural quality. This is a comparison of conditional associations, not a causal effect of role type.
design.unit: Player-move (mover-season). Only the player-level unit is considered here; team-season or single-game units would not reproduce the SF-CHT-057 design.
design.sample: Not feasible with n=24. The minimum viable test requires pooling mover-seasons across 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons and playoffs to approach the scale of the closest prior study (n about 90 movers). If the pool falls well short, stop and report the question as untestable.
design.power: Pre-specify the MDE at 80% power before any outcome is examined, using the SD from the pooled sample. Based on SF-APPS-024 (SD about 0.34), a 24-unit design has MDE well above any plausible effect. Proceed only if the pooled MDE is below the effect size reported in SF-CHT-057 (AUC about 0.65, about one-third of a tercile difference).
design.controls: Destination structural quality (landing-spot net rating or structural-gap index measured before the move, not after); pre-move minutes and usage; team pace; position; season; and playoff versus regular-season indicator. Role classification thresholds fixed from pre-move data only, not from outcomes. Measurement reliability of cut and drive shares reported across seasons.
design.falsification: Placebo outcome: pre-move function delta (change in function before the move, when no move occurs). Permutation of portability labels preserving team and destination structure. Pre-specified negative control: the same cut-versus-drive contrast on non-movers should show no association.
design.multiplicity: One primary contrast (cut-minus-drive share vs portability). Tercile, position, and drop-one-player checks are secondary and are reported with Holm correction across the secondary set.
design.decision_rule: Support only if the pre-specified primary contrast is significant after Holm correction across the pre-registered secondary checks, the effect survives destination-quality adjustment, and the placebo and non-mover controls show no association. Reject if the pooled MDE is below the plausible effect and the observed effect is null. Report untestable if the pooled sample is below the MDE threshold.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, plus 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) and 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21). Any pull before those completion dates is partial and must not be used. Derived play-type possession records must be rebuilt from play-by-play with a fixed coding version.

methodological_questions: Can role transferability be tested with n=24 units?
How should cut-heavy and drive-heavy shaper roles be classified from play-by-play data?
What sample size, exposure and reliability thresholds apply when comparing role portability across seasons and playoffs?
How should regression to the mean and label derivation from outcomes be controlled?
args.query: Cut-heavy shapers roles travel better than drive-heavy ones: prior studies on structural roles, influence, play-type classification, and cross-context transfer of player roles in NBA play-by-play data 2022-23 to 2025-26

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24
